## Round g1r2: profile after E0001 (operator CPU)
- HASH_GROUP_BY 0.31-0.79s (distinct HT only; CanSkipRegularSink skips the main sink when all aggs are DISTINCT).
- Distinct HT key: p_brand compressed to uhugeint, p_type raw VARCHAR (heap), p_size utinyint, plus suppkey.
- partsupp scan 0.20-0.29s (8M rows, min/max + hashed BF, emits 1.236M; the join keeps 1.185M).

- E0003 RETIRED: sparse perfect HJ + BF +39..56%. Serial 66MB dictionary build. Bad idea for wide payloads.
- RULE: divide EXPLAIN ANALYZE operator CPU by 8 for a wall-time estimate before predicting gains.
- Perfect HJ: range cap 1M (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:108); dup check off by one; a perfect HJ disables the BF.

## Round g1r4
- E0004 RETIRED (not implemented): distinct finalize CPU: distinct GetData 150-168ms, main-HT sink 104ms, Combine 1.5ms. Group-aligned main sink <=3.5%.
- Combine resets the local HT; the next Sink re-allocates the full pointer table.
- Debug tip: Printer::Print output shows up as "ERROR:" on stderr from dbe-tool sql.

## Round g1r5
- E0005 RETIRED: staging gate for heap layouts (AllConstant at aggregate_hashtable.cpp:755): -5.7% visible, rejected as noise. Third attempt overall (-6.5, -7.7 in the implementer's runs). A real but marginal gain; only worth stacking with something else.

## Round g1r6
- Dispatched: exact bitmap BF for dense-int keys (bloom_filter.hpp/.cpp, PushBloomFilter physical_hash_join.cpp:787, deferred push :587, min/max at :862; BLOOM_FILTER eval at column_segment.cpp:558, table_scan.cpp:498, table_filter_state.cpp:16). Expected -4..-8%.
- Fresh profile (0.30s total with profiling on): HASH_GROUP_BY 0.79s CPU, INNER HJ 0.27s, partsupp scan 0.29s, part scan 0.07s, everything else <=0.04s.

## Remaining levers for q16 (if a future generation continues)
- Count DISTINCT directly from group-aligned distinct partitions (backlog; removes ~104ms CPU of main sink, ~7% max; medium-high risk in the distinct finalize protocol, AggregateDistinctGrouping physical_hash_aggregate.cpp:665).
- p_type VARCHAR in the distinct HT key (>16 bytes, so no CM compression): dictionary-ID group keys would avoid the heap layout. Largest potential but invasive.
- Stacking the staging gate (E0005) with another win.

issues.title: Exact bitmap BF for dense-int join keys on partsupp-style probes
issues.hypothesis: Fresh profile of q16.m0: the partsupp TABLE_SCAN costs 0.20-0.29s CPU (25-36ms wall at 8 threads, 15-20% of the query). It probes 8M rows through min/max plus a hashed BloomFilter and emits 1,236,280 rows, but the INNER join keeps only 1,185,556, so ~51k rows are false positives that the join (0.22-0.27s CPU incl. scan) has to probe. The build key p_partkey-style column is a dense integer: 296k keys selected out of a ~2M range, so a bitmap over [min,max] needs ~2M bits = 250KB, which is about 7 bits per key and stays cache-friendly. The bitmap test (key-min, shift, and) replaces hashing every probe value plus a sector lookup, and it has zero false positives. In earlier db_evolve runs on this engine the same mechanism gave q09 -9.5..-14% and q21 -15%. This tree has only the hashed BloomFilter (bloom_filter.hpp:20).
issues.plan: 1) In src/include/duckdb/planner/filter/bloom_filter.hpp and src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp, add an exact-bitmap mode to BloomFilter, or a sibling class used by BFTableFilter: base value (int64 or hugeint), range, vector<uint64_t> bits, plus InsertKeys(Vector&, count) and LookupKeys(Vector&, sel, count). Handle integral physical types via templates. 2) In physical_hash_join.cpp, PushBloomFilter (~line 787) and the deferred path in Finalize (~line 587): when the key type is integral, there is no cast, the HT key min/max is known (the min/max is already computed at ~line 862), and (max-min+1) <= 128 * ht.Count() (cap at 2^27 bits), fill the bitmap by scanning the build key column instead of hashing. Reuse the existing ScanKeyColumn-style path; E0003 notes say it works. 3) In the scan filter evaluation for TableFilterType::BLOOM_FILTER (column_segment.cpp:558, table_scan.cpp:498, table_filter_state.cpp:16), when the filter is in exact mode, skip HashInternal and test bits directly. Values outside [min,max] are rejected. NULLs follow filters_null_values. Keep the hashed BF as the fallback for every other case. Display the filter as 'IN BF' unchanged, or as 'IN BITMAP'.
issues.expected_gain: q16 -4..-8%: the partsupp scan drops from ~30ms wall toward ~15-20ms, and the join probes ~51k fewer rows.
issues.generality: Any hash join on dense integer surrogate keys with a selective build side (star and snowflake fact-dimension joins, TPC-H lineitem/partsupp/orders probes). Joins on sparse keys fall back to the hashed BF and are unchanged. The only extra cost is the bitmap build, bounded by the 128 bits/key cap.
issues.risk: Medium. The diff is larger. Correctness depends on exact min/max and on the signed/unsigned and hugeint handling of key-min. Without a cap on the bitmap size, a huge range could cost memory and build time. Serialization of BFTableFilter must either keep working or treat the exact mode as non-serializable, as dynamic filters are.
